title: Cyrus and the Ledger
premise: Ines Oyelaran, coroner of the fading town of Marrow Creek, discovers that the diary of missing schoolteacher Ada Voss contains entries written after her disappearance — entries in Ines's own handwriting, which she has no memory of writing. Following the ledger's clues, she uncovers a thirty-year-old cover-up: three 'accidental' deaths were murders committed to protect the town's founding families, and her late father was both witness and accomplice. As the true killer closes in, Ines must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the last living person who loved her father. In the end she testifies, burning the ledger's final page so the town can bury its dead honestly at last.
about_author: Lena Thackeray is the pen name of a former rural hospice nurse who spent a decade recording other people's final stories. She writes mysteries about small towns where everyone remembers everything except what matters.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She buries old Tom Aldous, officially a heart attack, though she suspects otherwise, and reflects on the three deaths she quietly solved that police called accidents. Establishes her loneliness, her meticulous ledgers, and her loyalty to the dead. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking grief.

chapters.title: The Voss File
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sheriff's deputy Dana Ruiz asks Ines to formally close the Ada Voss missing-person case; Ada vanished eleven years ago. Ines refuses to sign until she can inventory Ada's stored belongings. Beat: stubbornness as principle, first friction with authority.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sorting Ada's boxes in the evidence annex, Ines finds Ada's diary — and entries continuing two years past her disappearance, describing conversations with Ines herself. The handwriting on the final pages is unmistakably Ines's own. Beat: vertigo, self-doubt, the ground tilting.

chapters.title: What I Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with diary excerpts. She checks her own journals for those dates and finds pages razored out. Her sleep fractures; she begins dreaming of the creek behind the old Harrow mill. Beat: fear turned inward, memory as unreliable terrain.

chapters.title: The Mill Road Alibi
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She interviews Wendell Harrow, patriarch of the mill family, who offers an airtight alibi for the night Ada vanished — one he has clearly rehearsed for decades. His son Marcus watches from the stairs. Beat: polished lies, first sense of real danger.

chapters.title: Dana's Doubts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Deputy Dana Ruiz. Dana admits off-record that three cold cases bother her too, but warns Ines that the Harrows fund half the county. An uneasy alliance forms. Beat: loyalty tested between badge and conscience.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In her father's effects she finds a second ledger — payments recorded over thirty years from H. Harrow to E. Oyelaran. Her father took money to stay silent about something. Beat: betrayal across the grave, love and anger entangled.

chapters.title: Ada's Last Semester
chapters.summary: Ines's POV with flashbacks reconstructed from the diary. Ada had been tutoring a Harrow grandchild and stumbled onto records of a 1994 death ruled accidental: a worker crushed at the mill. Beat: the past acquiring weight and shape.

chapters.title: Someone Rearranges My Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Returning home, Ines finds the diary moved and a fresh entry added: STOP ASKING WHO WROTE THIS. The intruder knows her routines. Beat: violation, paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She tracks down Ruthie Callow, Ada's former colleague, now living alone outside town. Ruthie reveals Ada came to her frightened the week she disappeared — and that Ruthie saw Ines's truck near the mill that night. Beat: the trap tightening around someone she trusts.

chapters.title: Truck, Keys, Blank Hours
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Forensics on her own vehicle turn up mill dust and a torn diary page fragment under the seat. Dana must open a file naming Ines as a person of interest. Beat: the horror of being evidence against yourself.

chapters.title: Marcus Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Marcus Harrow visits, ostensibly to offer condolences about her father, actually to probe how much she knows. He mentions her father's debts with soft menace. Beat: charm as a weapon, the reader seeing what Ines almost misses.

chapters.title: The Third Grave
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Exhuming a body she buried years ago — the mill worker's widow, another 'accident' — Ines confirms antemortem injuries consistent with murder. Three deaths, one pattern, all signed off by her predecessors. Beat: righteous fury, the case becoming hers.

chapters.title: Ruthie Recants
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ruthie retracts her statement, terrified, then privately slips Ines a photograph: young Wendell, her father, and the 1994 victim together at the mill. Beat: courage flickering under pressure, an inheritance of silence.

chapters.title: What My Father Carried
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, interleaved with her father's letters. She learns he witnessed the 1994 killing, took hush money to pay her mother's medical bills, and spent his life keeping the ledger — including notes on Ada's investigation. Beat: understanding without absolution; the theme of survival's price made personal.

chapters.title: The Missing Night
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A hypnotist-adjacent memory exercise with a retired forensic psychologist surfaces fragments: Ines did drive to the mill the night Ada vanished — summoned by an anonymous note — and saw a figure by the water before her memory blanks. Beat: dread and hope braided together.

chapters.title: Ledger, Final Page
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Deciphering her father's shorthand, she finds the ledger's last entry, dated after his death, in her own handwriting again: ADA IS ALIVE. OR WAS. The diary entries were coerced — Ines was drugged and made to copy text, a lever to control her if her father's records ever surfaced. Beat: revelation reframing every prior chapter.

chapters.title: Creek Water Rising
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following the ledger's coordinates to the flooded quarry behind the mill, she finds Ada's remains — and evidence she died recently, not eleven years ago. Someone kept her captive for years. Beat: grief curdling into purpose; the clock now runs backward.

chapters.title: The Confession Room
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Confronting Wendell, she springs the trap: the drug used on her matches prescriptions only he could obtain, and the diary's coercion dates align with his 'alibi.' Wendell breaks — Ada discovered the 1994 murder and he couldn't risk freedom twice. Beat: climax of intellect, evil revealed as banal self-preservation.

chapters.title: Marcus's Choice
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Marcus, holding the ledger's original, offers Ines a deal: burn it, protect the family name, and her father's complicity dies with it. She chooses truth over loyalty — the book's thematic crux — and hands the ledger to Dana. Beat: sacrifice, the cost counted honestly.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, courtroom and aftermath. She testifies through the drug-induced gaps, owning her lost nights without shame. Wendell is convicted; Marcus walks on technicalities but leaves town. Beat: catharsis, justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Names on Stone
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She carves accurate causes onto her private register, burns the ledger's final page as promised, and visits Ada's new headstone — speaking aloud the names of every grave she keeps. Beat: resolution, memory honored, the survivor carrying the weight willingly.
